task_intent: Refine five Tessera music, conversation and arcade games with expressive native boards and matching wall compositions.

references.observed: User and assistant turns have distinct hierarchy, thinking status sits inline, and the previous exchange remains available during a response.
references.applied: A numbered question card sits above persistent yes/sort-of/no controls, with an acknowledged conversation trail. Provider thinking and retry stay inline without losing previously recorded answers.

references.observed: A broad illustrative canvas takes priority, while the activity title, one clear action and elapsed/total timing remain separate and legible.
references.applied: The streamed Pictionary picture is the central full-resolution canvas. The guess field, timer and drawing status stay outside it; completed art remains unobscured.

references.observed: Inline feedback communicates current status, success, failure and recoverable mistakes without interrupting the surrounding task.
references.applied: Answers receive their own receipt and question token; stale answers are rejected. Provider failures preserve the round and offer one explicit retry instead of recording a loss.

references.observed: Unknown-duration work should use indeterminate activity feedback; known-duration activity can expose meaningful progress, with actionable recovery for a stalled operation.
references.applied: Drawing uses a pencil motif and activity indicator until a partial image arrives. The real round timer starts with that first image, continues through final generation, and freezes at completion. Failed generation can retry without starting a phantom timer.

references.observed: Action labels should make the next action clear, and copy should account for the available screen space.
references.applied: Explicit answer, retry and guess labels accompany symbols. Larger text stacks controls and presents the complete question; wall microcopy shortens at64 while the complete question remains available through paged lines.

implementation.twentyq: Async provider requests commit under the host lock only while the game owns its session; generation IDs discard stale completions. Native answers send question_id; legacy tokenless answers remain supported. Full history is retained and expands inline.
implementation.pictionary: Provider callbacks publish copied512px masters with ownership checks. Late partials/finals/errors cannot reopen finished rounds; retries retain the secret, strict whole-name matching supports ordinary plurals, and correct answers freeze elapsed time.

validation.python_tests: 65 passed across test_twentyq.py, test_pictionary.py and test_conversation_batch.py
validation.swift_syntax: Both owned Swift files passed swiftc frontend parse
